text:
maria: quick heads-up — the lyra20b int4 canary (v0.9.1-quant) is showing a small but persistent quality droprate on long contexts and a few OOMs during multi-turn sessions. collected traces attached below.

sam: saw the same on a couple traces, droprate ~2.7% on long-chat eval set vs 1.1% baseline. OOMs correlate with sessions that hit max_new_tokens=512.

quinn: interesting — were we defaulting max_new_tokens higher in the canary route? I thought default was 256.

maria: yeah that's the weird part. route config had no explicit max_new_tokens so the new service default (recent patch) bumped it to 512 for this model profile. guess it exposed fragmentation under int4.

ops: deploy-bot: Canary deploy lyra20b-int4 v0.9.1-quant -> pool-canary-3 completed at 1701234700 :white_check_mark:

quinn: logs from one OOM run (trimmed):
```
[2024-10-28T21:12:47Z] runtime: allocation failed: cudaMalloc returned OOM
model=lyra20b-int4 shard=1 seq=4096 max_new=512
KVCache reserve attempt: 1 -> evict candidates: 0.
trace: allocate prefetched kv pages -> failed
```

sasha: kv eviction didn't trigger? maybe our eviction threshold for int4 got tighter after the quant packing change. also int4 kernels are chunking memory differently.

sam: hypothesis: raising default max_new_tokens -> larger ephemeral allocation per request -> higher KV churn -> fragmentation + failing cudaMalloc. two mitigations: lower default max_new_tokens on this route OR enable soft-evict before alloc.

maria: did a quick test locally with max_new_tokens=256 and soft_eviction=true, microbatch=1; no OOMs in 200 long-chat sims. quality droprate? still +1.5% vs baseline, so quantization quality regression separate.

quinn: can you paste the route snippet you used?

maria: route config we used:
```json
{
  "route": "lyra20b-int4-canary",
  "model_variant": "lyra20b-int4-v0.9.1-quant",
  "defaults": {
    "max_new_tokens": 256,
    "microbatch_size": 1,
    "soft_eviction": true,
    "prefetch": "balanced"
  }
}
```

sasha: good. for fragmentation we also want to enable kv_trim_interval=30s on the canary nodes — frees orphaned KV segments. last time that helped with warmup churn.

ops: putting kv_trim_interval=30s into the canary config now, will monitor for the next hour.

deploy-bot: Update applied to lyra20b-int4-canary at 1701234810 by ops.

sam: on the quality side I ran an eval comparing v0.9.1-quant to v0.8.7 (float16 baseline). small but consistent drop on instruction-following prompts that require longer planning. suspect mixing per-layer rounding + EOS handling on int4.

quinn: can we do a targeted rollback of quant bits on last transformer block or restore fp16 for the LM head as an experiment? trade memory for quality.

maria: plan: 1) immediate config change to default max_new_tokens=256 + soft_eviction + kv_trim_interval to stop OOMs; 2) run two bench jobs: (A) per-layer hybrid quant (last 2 layers fp16) (B) fp16 head only. measure droprate + latency cost. 3) if (A) recovers quality at <6% memory delta, consider canary v0.9.2-hybrid.

sasha: add a small eval set with long-plan prompts (15-20 tokens instruction, expecting 200+ generation) — that's where we saw regression. I'll push sets to /evals/lyra20b/longplan.

ops: ops note: if we lower max_new_tokens route-wide, ensure the console default for self-serve remains unchanged or document the canary override so customers aren't surprised.

maria: agree. will add a console banner for canary noting the temporary limit and the reason. also tagging support in case customers hit it.

sam: quick command to run the hybrid quant bench (use bench runner):
```bash
bench-run --model lyra20b --variant int4 --hybrid-layers tail:2 --evals /evals/lyra20b/longplan --out /tmp/bench-hybrid.json
```

quinn: thanks. I'll queue that and the head-fp16 run. also instrument token-level drop logging (compare probs at token boundaries) so we can tell if the model is truncating or low-confidence.

maria: tl;dr actionables: [ops] applied kv_trim and will monitor; [maria/sam/quinn] run hybrid + head-fp16 benches; [sasha] push longplan evals; [maria] console banner + support note. will reconvene in ~2h with bench results.

ops: note: observed one minor latency bump (p95 +14ms) after kv_trim enabled, probably background compaction, will keep an eye.

maria: thanks all. posting the key traces and a zipped canary trace here: https://internal.artifacts/lyra20b/canary-traces/1701234567.zip

deploy-bot: Alert: canary pool usage increased by 8% after config change at 1701234860.

quinn: ok good to pause here. we'll post bench outputs in this thread.

sasha: bringing in model-owner (cc @matt) on quality regression once we have bench numbers.

maria: sounds good — pinging when benches complete.
